messages:
alex_lee: Customer (ACME EU) opened a ticket — they see spikes in latency and a bunch of 401 auth failures from eu endpoints starting ~08:30 UTC. They say traces show requests landing in us-east-1. attaching snippet from their app logs.

maria_garcia: Can you paste a sample request/response (headers + auth token truncated) and the IP they saw?

alex_lee: Here. token=Xxx... (redacted). client IP observed by customer: 185.45.22.10. sample response: 
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2024 08:34:12 GMT
x-redwood-region: us-east-1
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "token_mismatch"
}

jordan_rm: Noting x-redwood-region header — looks like the request was routed to us-east. That would explain auth token scope if the token was issued for eu clusters.

samir_k: Did anything change with GeoIP or DNS config? I deployed GeoIP DB refresh yesterday morning via infra pipeline. ops-bot: (deployment) geolite2-db updated to 2024-04-25 on all edges at 06:10 UTC.

maria_garcia: Could be ISP/resolver caches still serving old anycast mapping. Ask customer to run dig +trace and traceroute to our endpoint and paste results. Also get the resolver IP (e.g., 1.2.3.4). TTLs matter.

alex_lee: Customer ran these. dig +short returned 52.16.12.34 (us-east) from their resolver. dig +trace shows authoritative answer changed, but their recursive resolver has a cached A with 8h TTL left. Paste below:

;; ANSWER SECTION:
example.redwood.ai. 28800 IN A 52.16.12.34
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood.ai. 3600 IN NS ns-eu-1.redwood.ai.

traceroute to example.redwood.ai (52.16.12.34), 30 hops max:
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  isp-edge  12 ms
 3  ...
 7  52.16.12.34  120 ms

alex_lee: Customer says they didn't change resolvers. They mention their corporate DNS appliance is managed by an ISP partner.

jordan_rm: Classic stale resolver cache + anycast flip. If the edge announced different anycast mapping after GeoIP update, resolvers that cached previous A will keep hitting the old region.

maria_garcia: That also explains multiple retries: their app retries on 401 and sometimes the next attempt goes to eu and succeeds -> billing duplicates and confused auth flow. Customer sees duplicate token use and spike in invoices.

samir_k: Quick mitigation for them: 1) Use a region pin header (we have x-redwood-region to force eu-west) 2) Use a dedicated EU endpoint (dedicated-*.eu.redwood.ai) if on Dedicated or Private plans 3) switch to public resolvers (8.8.8.8) or ask ISP to flush cache.

alex_lee: Sent those to the customer. They replied that they cannot change resolvers quickly — corporate policy. They asked if we can do anything server-side.

eng-infra: Pinged. Possible server-side mitigations: 1) honor x-cc/geoip hints when present 2) extend sticky fallbacks so auth tokens are accepted cross-region for short window to avoid 401 on flapping routes 3) add warning in response instead of 401 when token region mismatch detected (requires product consent).

jordan_rm: Also want to verify if our caching layer is respecting EDNS Client Subnet (ECS). Some ISP resolvers strip ECS -> wrong geolocation. If ECS was added in the GeoIP rollout, older cached entries could direct to the wrong POP.

samir_k: Ops note — seen this before with ISP X in Germany. Their recursive caches were honoring old anycast prefixes for 48 hours. Recommend we add a fallback route that checks token region and prefers routing to matching region if possible (best-effort), rather than returning 401 immediately. Escalating to eng-runtime for feasibility.

eng-infra: Logging task created: INFRA-3789. Need packet captures + exact resolver IPs to reproduce in lab. Suggested repro steps for customer: 
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://example.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -o /tmp/resp.txt
2) dig +short example.redwood.ai @their-resolver-ip; dig +trace example.redwood.ai
3) tcpdump -nni any host example.redwood.ai and port 443 (run for 60s)
4) paste /tmp/resp.txt and tcpdump pcap to support ticket.

alex_lee: Customer provided resolver IP 89.22.11.7 and pcap. Uploaded to ticket. Their pcap shows SYN/ACK to 52.16.12.34 (us-east).

maria_garcia: Thanks. Set expected next steps: eng-infra to try to repro with chained resolvers (simulate stale cache), eng-runtime to evaluate token-relaxation fallback. Support to notify billing about potential duplicate charge window.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20240426-47 — Region routing mismatch impacting EU customer routing. Priority: P2.

jordan_rm: One more note — TTLs on our A records were too high during the GeoIP swap (we had a 28800 default). For future maintenance we should reduce TTL pre-swap to 300s and raise again afterward. Filed RFC: RFC-geoip-swap-2024.

samir_k: Agreed. I'll draft a short runbook for customers and our support ops describing steps to mitigate (region pin header, resolvers, how to capture traces).

alex_lee: Customer accepted temporary workaround (x-redwood-region header) for now and will work with their ISP to flush cache. They're worried about billing spike; I asked billing to hold charges until we verify duplicates.

eng-infra: Will post repro results by EOD. If anyone sees more customers with same resolver IP prefix, flag here.

maria_garcia: Thx team. Closing loop when infra posts findings. :thumbsup:
